name: Blackstrap Provincial Park - Hazelnut Grove Campground
waterfront_evidence: Split 2026-11-19. Esri World_Imagery z18 (0.37 m/px, and a 2x crop) with all 19 SKPP GIS site points: the lake-side row (100-101, 103-105, 108-110, 112, 114-117) sits about 10-25 m from Blackstrap Lake's open water behind a continuous band of shoreline willow, shrubs and trees (pixel profiles: vegetation to open water at about 12-22 m from 109, 110 and 117; on the reservoir the vegetated edge is the high-water line); 102, 106, 107, 111, 113 and 118 sit across the loop road in woods. SKPP site photos (read 2026-11-19): the lake shows through or over shrubs from 100, 101, 103, 104, 108, 109, 116 and 117, not from the rest; no site on open ground to the water. Every paging row reads 'Near Water - no'; the loop's area note speaks of 'lakefront sites' (an algae-odour warning) - re-audited on imagery and photos: a screened view, not on the water. --Claude
inclusion_evidence: ReserveAmerica SKPP parkId 290310, Hazelnut Grove loop, read 2026-11-19 (paging table + every site's detail page): 19 site-specific Nightly Electric sites 100-118, all 15/30 A, back-in (113 roadside); 'Maximum Equipment Length (ft)' 25-40, but 'Allowed Equipment' takes a 19-25 ft unit on 17 sites (100 also 26-40 ft; 102 and 106 a tent or van/truck camper only); area note 'Sites are small and better suited for small campers under 25 feet.' Park map (2026-04-10) draws it on its own spur by the park entrance with potable water and washrooms. Runs the park's winter camping. A real public drive-in RV campground a 23-ft rig fits. --Claude
note: The park's lakeshore loop by the entrance, about 5 km north of the Kevin Misfeldt and Sunset Ridge campgrounds (own entry); no showers or dump station here. Small wooded sites: most book online only for a unit up to 25 ft, and 102 and 106 only for a tent or van camper. Algae blooms in hot weather can bring a strong smell. --Claude

season.note: 2026-27 dates. Summer season May 14 to September 30; winter camping November 1 to March 14 on electric sites with pit toilets, no water, showers or dump station. October nights are booked through the park.

fees.note: $4 a night less from October 1, with reduced services.
